Turn in all of your notes and event materials when you have completed the event.
situation:
You are the marketing director (participant one) and the compliance manager (participant two) at BRIGHTKEEL IMPORTS, an importer of wooden and plush toys for children under eight. The chief executive officer (judge) took over eighteen months ago, after two losing years, and has asked the two of you to meet about a decision that cannot wait until after the holiday buying season.

BRIGHTKEEL buys from small workshops in three countries and sells to independent toy shops and one regional chain. Most of the recovery has come from a short-video channel built by the digital content manager, whose clips of real children playing with the toys are now the first touch point for nearly every new customer. The chain's buyer said plainly that the channel is why the account was signed.

Company policy, written after last year's audit, requires a signed parental release before any identifiable child appears in company content. The digital content manager filmed the current holiday series at a public toy fair, where posted signage disclosed recording, and collected no releases. Counsel has confirmed that the footage was lawfully obtained and may stay online. Nothing about the videos is illegal; the policy the company wrote for itself is what was broken.

Parents who buy from BRIGHTKEEL are the people most likely to object to a toy company using children's faces without asking first. Pulling the series would strip the channel of its strongest library three weeks before the season, and the chain's buyer may revisit the account terms the company's finance manager negotiated while servicing that client. Leaving it up and disciplining quietly tells a staff of forty which rules are optional, and leaves the written policy standing as a promise the company did not keep.

The chief executive officer (judge) wants a recommendation on both halves of the problem: what happens to the video series, and what happens to a high performer whose work carried the turnaround. Explain how buying behavior and the company's customer touch points bear on the choice, what discipline is warranted, and the steps that would keep the same failure from happening again.

You will present your recommendation to the chief executive officer (judge) in a meeting in the executive's office. The chief executive officer (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the chief executive officer's questions, the chief executive officer (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief executive officer (judge) of BRIGHTKEEL IMPORTS. Business background is the same as the situation above. You were brought in after two losing years, and the short-video channel built by the digital content manager is the largest single reason the company is profitable again. You also signed the content policy that the digital content manager did not follow, and counsel has told you the footage is lawful and may remain online.

You want the participant team to recommend what to do with the video series and what discipline, if any, the digital content manager should receive. You want to hear how customers are likely to react, which touch points are affected, what the recommendation costs the company in the weeks before the season, and what steps would prevent a repeat.

During the course of the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant team:
judgeQuestions: Six months from now, how would we know we made the right call?
What would tell us that people here still take the policy seriously?
